'''Martin Laurence Fick''' (30 November 1898 – 2 August 1945) was a South African [[psychologist]] and [[psychometrician]]. He is noted for his work administering [[intelligence test]]s to South African children. On the basis of this research, he concluded that native South African children were intellectually inferior to their European counterparts, in support of the South African government's policy at the time of not investing in native children's education.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Hans |first=Nicholas |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Ad5g7vr3k28C&pg=PA33 |title=Comparative Education |publisher=Routledge |year=2011 |isbn=978-0415664288 |page=33}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Long |first=Graham Mark |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=kM2Oor_cdGgC&pg=PA172 |title=Relativism and the Foundations of Liberalism |date=2004 |publisher=Imprint Academic |isbn=978-1-84540-004-0 |pages=172 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Pillay |first=Anthony L |date=September 2019 |title=South Africa's phoenix rising from the ashes of apartheid Psychology: The Psychological Society of South Africa 25 years on |journal=South African Journal of Psychology |language=en |volume=49 |issue=3 |pages=305–307 |doi=10.1177/0081246319866968 |issn=0081-2463|doi-access=free }}</ref>

Fick graduated from the [[University of the Cape of Good Hope]] with a [[Bachelor of Arts|B. A.]] degree in 1917 and received his [[Master of Education|Ed. M.]] degree from [[Harvard University]] in 1922.<ref>{{Cite book |last=University |first=Harvard |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=jPgYAQAAIAAJ&pg=PP394 |title=The Harvard University Catalogue |publisher=University |year=1922 |pages=292 |language=en}}</ref> In 1926, Fick published the Official Mental Hygiene Individual Scale (also known as the "Fick Scale"), which was the first South African intelligence test.<ref name="introduction" /><ref>{{Cite book |last=Baker |first=David B. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=I5FoAgAAQBAJ&pg=PA498 |title=The Oxford Handbook of the History of Psychology: Global Perspectives |date=2012-01-13 |publisher=Oxford University Press |isbn=978-0-19-971065-2 |pages=498 |language=en}}</ref> Fick worked for the [[National Bureau of Educational and Social Research]], and was noted for his [[hereditarian]] interpretation of racial differences in intelligence test scores. This interpretation was criticized by other psychologists such as [[Simon Biesheuvel]].<ref name="introduction">{{Cite book |last=Nicholas |first=Lionel |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=MP5X2SK2DCgC&pg=PA169 |title=Introduction to Psychology |year=2009 |publisher=Juta and Company Ltd |isbn=978-1-919895-02-4 |pages=169 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Desai |first=Gaurav |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=dyPXuWaJWD0C&pg=PA39 |title=Subject to Colonialism: African Self-Fashioning and the Colonial Library |date=2001-06-20 |publisher=Duke University Press |isbn=978-0-8223-2641-0 |pages=39 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=RpopAQAAIAAJ |title=ALA Bulletin: A Publication of the African Literature Association |publisher=African Literature Association |year=2001 |pages=127 |language=en}}</ref> Fick was also a captain in the [[South African Medical Corps]], and he died in 1945 while serving on active duty.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Fick, Martin Laurence |url=http://www.southafricawargraves.org/search/print.php?id=7102 |access-date=2020-06-14 |website=South African War Graves Project}}</ref>
